reader.requirement: At --std 85, any statement in a program directly or indirectly contained in the program that declares a global name (data-name, its subordinates and condition-names, file-name, report-name, index-name) must reference that name without redescribing it, resolving to the container's object by the X.1.3.8.2 rules (own name first, then the nearest container's global), while a containing program, or a separately compiled program, gets no access to it.
reader.edition-search: read SymbolTable.NearestDeclaring, DataBinder.InheritContainerGlobalData/InheritGlobalSubtree and InheritedGlobals.AddContainerFiles; grep of Edition/DialectLevel/CobolVersion/Edition.Has over SymbolTable.cs, LinkageBinder.cs, InheritStep.cs and InheritedGlobals.cs found none. The edition-dependent arms near this path belong to other rules (LINAGE-COUNTER's qualification count, LINKAGE GLOBAL).
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness covers name resolution (local first, nearest container's global, qualification through a nearer global group, index-name hidden by a local data-name) in a two-level nest; not exercised: a variable-length GLOBAL record with a global ODO object the containee changes, reference modification at its bounds, a PERFORM loop whose global subscript the statement changes, I-O statements on GLOBAL files from an indirect containee (a failed OPEN with a global FILE STATUS, then WRITE), and the refusal for a container referencing a containee's GLOBAL name and for a separately compiled program. All probed here.

probes.expected: §1985:X.1.3.8.2: a program cannot reference a name declared in a program it contains, and a global name reaches only the declaring program and its containees: both refused

reader.notes: Container GLOBAL subtrees are inherited into each containee's name set with their declaring depth, and NearestDeclaring narrows a plural candidate set to the nearest declaring element, which is X.1.3.8.2 rule 3. The cells stay the container's and are reached through the GLOBAL bridge, so writes are seen by the container. No edition is consulted on this path.

refuter.evidence: gn1.cob (run gn1-002, --std 85; gn1-001 was refused for my missing AT END, COBOL6826, a correct 1985 refusal): A declares GLOBAL X, GLOBAL group G with Y and 88 Y-IS-AY, and GLOBAL FD XF. Its containee B declares a LOCAL X, Y, 88 Y-IS-AY and a local FD XF of the same names. D, inside B, references them all without describing them. Printed 'D X=OUTER Y=AY / D Y-IS-AY TRUE / D WRITE 00 / B X=MIDDL Y=BY / A X=DSET Y=DY / A READ 00 ARC1', and only GN1AX.DAT was written. D's name set holds its own names and the containers' GLOBAL names only (X.1.3.8.2 GR1), so B's local homonyms are not candidates: the data-names, the condition-name and the file-name all resolve to A's objects. D's MOVEs and WRITE land in A's cells and file, and B keeps its own. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:X.4.6.4 GR2 ... the text is in GR2'; 'OK  §1985:X.1.3.8.2 ... it lies in GR1'.
